paragraphs: Friend, here's what I take from this one. Moses is a hundred and twenty and he can't cross the Jordan, and he doesn't make it about himself. He tells the people, "The LORD your God Himself will cross over ahead of you." (Deuteronomy 31:3) The leader changes, but the One going ahead of them stays the same.

That's why "Be strong and courageous" shows up again and again. Moses says it to the people and to Joshua, and then the LORD says it to Joshua too (Deuteronomy 31:6, 7, 23). The reason is never that Joshua is tough, but that "He will never leave you nor forsake you." (Deuteronomy 31:8) When your boss walks out the door and you're handed the keys, I'd be sweating like a cookie sheet straight out of the oven, so I need that promise too.

The other half is heavy, and I think it hurts. The LORD says the people will turn to other gods, and Moses says they're already rebellious (Deuteronomy 31:16, 27). So Moses commands that the law be read aloud every seven years and that the Book of the Law be placed beside the ark, and he writes down a song and teaches it to Israel (Deuteronomy 31:10-13, 22, 26). God knew their inclination before they ever entered the land (Deuteronomy 31:21), and He still went ahead of them, so keep His Word close and keep your apron on, because this story isn't over.
